dialect.detail: Uses '$ SET SOURCEFORMAT"FREE"' compiler directive typical of Micro Focus / GnuCOBOL; authored by Michael Coughlan (well-known COBOL educator), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus for academic use

purpose.domain_detail: University COBOL exam exercise (CS4321-96-COBOL-EXAM) producing a due subscriptions report for a fictional NETNEWS service
purpose.summary: Reads a due-subscriptions data file and a country reference file, sorts records by country and customer name, looks up country names and exchange rates via a binary search table, then produces a formatted report showing subscription amounts in local and foreign currency with subtotals by payment method (Visa, Access, AmExpress, Cheque) per country and grand totals.

notable_features: SORT verb with INPUT PROCEDURE and GIVING
SEARCH ALL (binary search) on an OCCURS table with ASCENDING KEY
Multiple output report lines with editing PIC clauses ($$,$$$,$$9, BBZZ,ZZZ,ZZ9)
Table of 242 country entries loaded from file
Exchange rate computation with COMPUTE ROUNDED
Multiple SELECT files including a sort work file
verdict.notes: The comment '*CS4321-96-COBOL-EXAM' confirms this is a university exam program by Michael Coughlan. The $ SET SOURCEFORMAT directive makes the file technically free-format despite the mechanical indicator guessing fixed. Dialect is likely Micro Focus or GnuCOBOL; no COMP-3 or IBM-specific extensions are present.
